To leave comments and trace of deprecation, you can call it a bad habit of mine. But this particularly has confused me a lot:

`RSG::rasterizer::can_create_resources_async()` is a virtual function overridden by `rasterizer_gles3.h` and it simply returns `false`. This line was modified by PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/90400 and left untouched since then. Before that PR, it was `TextureStorage::can_create_resources_async()` and simply returns `true`

As far as I can tell this boolean is mainly used to determine if we initialize textures on thread or push to command queue at RenderingServer.

I did not dive deeper so I went with flipping this back to `true` here, and make all operations in this PR that's not thread-safe to be called on idle time using `call_deferred()` (creating scene, interact with main tree), and polish it out by testing, keep everything on thread as much as possible, move calls that causes issue to idle time.

I am not sure about the threading thing on web editor, I only know that somewhere between Godot 4.4 and 4.6 the pthread issue on iOS has been resolved and all web builds can be run on thread.

But I don't want to bet on it, I'll simply do:
```c++
bool EditorResourcePreview::can_run_on_thread() const {
#ifdef WEB_ENABLED
    return false;
#endif
    return true;
```
And force to use fallback thumbnails that just implemented. This might be the most feasible way as web editor has far less compute power and ... less people use it anyway.

Web builds with thread support do exist, however they are more difficult to serve, so non-threaded alternative exists too. Not sure which one is used by the editor tbh, but either way you should be checking `THREADS_ENABLED` instead.

Given that this PR is effectively undoing #87229 by once again putting the image creation for the Compatibility renderer on another thread, I would assume this would cause a regression of #87196, or some other problem? It would be great if @RandomShaper could chime in here.

In general I welcome some reduction of the 100 ms budget, since it still seems to make the web editor quite unresponsive on lower-end devices, but I'd be curious to see the impact on throughput from only processing a single resource per frame. I have a feeling that will drag the generation out for quite a while when importing bigger projects in the web editor on lower-end devices. This code also doesn't seem to take cache hits into account, so can presumably end up "wasting" an entire process frame, which seems unfortunate.

Also, seeing as how `processing_item` is cleared at the end of `_iterate`, which is only ever called from `_idle_callback` on the main thread, will it ever not be `is_empty()` in a non-threaded scenario?

This while loop is causing a high CPU load even on an entirely empty project. It's just looping indefinitely with no wait what so ever until the next frame is drawn. Whilst it does have the 3 second max, it's called often enough that it's basically always running even when nothing is happening. This behavior either needs to change, or some kind of small delay needs to be added to not peg the CPU at full speed during this loop.

False alarm, I had apparently at some point set both the `interface/editor/timers/low_processor_mode_sleep_usec` and `interface/editor/timers/unfocused_low_processor_mode_sleep_usec` to unreasonably low numbers which was causing the actual CPU spike here. Reverted those to their original values and the CPU is no longer being pegged (just mistakenly saw this loop as a potential continuous loop with nothing actually taking up enough time to not have it spin up the CPU by a lot)
